main_body: Red barn: a large tiled roof slope (rows 5-57) over a plank front wall with double doors and two small windows (rows 59-89), on a grey stone base
top_band: Cream/orange ridge line at rows 6-8 (L220 to 84), then the red tile roof slope at rows 9-55 (L72 with L110 tile highlights), closed at the front by a cream eave line at rows 56-57
evidence: The roof is drawn as a big sloped top surface, about 47 rows of scalloped tile. It has a light ridge line at the top and a light eave line at rows 56-57. A dark row (58) sits under the eave, which shades the wall below. The wall front (rows 59-89) has its own vertical plank shading. The doors and windows have dark inset frames, and the dormer is a small gabled slope with a recessed window. The roof slope reads as a top surface like the reference houses, and no receding side faces are drawn.

style.evidence: The outlines are tinted dark brown and red-brown (0% neutral dark edge pixels), so they are not near-black stickers. The roof has about 5 steps in a regular scallop pattern. The wall has only 2-3 red tones with plain vertical stripes, and the grey doors, window frames and base are nearly flat. Measured density is far below both references: 7 colours per tile against 11 and 18, and 23 distinct colours against 66 and 185. The roof tiles repeat mechanically, with no per-tile variation or speckle like the references. The wall has no plaster or stone grain. It looks thinner and flatter than the references next to them.
